markets.trend: Unchanged this run -- KRX is closed 24-27 Sep 2026 for the Chuseok holiday, so 23 Sep remains the latest session. KOSPI had closed at a fresh record 7,080.92 (+63.01pt, +0.90%) on 23 Sep, the third straight record-setting session, after spiking to an intraday high of 7,153 on NY-led AI/semiconductor strength; gains were pared into the close as position-adjustment ahead of the holiday took hold. Institutions were the only net buyer (+₩317.0bn) while both foreigners (-₩510.1bn) and retail (-₩1,439.7bn, the largest single-day retail outflow of that week) sold. Looking back one session further, foreign investors had flipped to net buying (+₩426.2bn) on 18 Sep after 7 straight sessions of selling (-₩14.58tn, 9-17 Sep), notably re-entering SK Hynix (+₩1.33tn) while trimming Samsung Electronics (-₩462bn).
markets.interpretation: A third consecutive record close on institution-only buying, with both foreign and retail investors de-risking ahead of a 4-day market closure, reads as pre-holiday position trimming rather than a change in trend. Korean commentary (Yuanta and others) frames the pre-holiday dip as a potential buying opportunity if foreign net buying continues and oil/rates stay stable, citing seasonality (KOSPI averages -0.42% in the 5 sessions before Chuseok but +0.68% after) -- though that seasonality pattern predates this weekend's Iran-Hormuz escalation, which is a fresh headwind not reflected in it. KRX also launches extended after-hours trading (until 8pm) starting Monday 28 Sep, a structural change that may draw more foreign participation going forward. Monday's reopen is the key tell for whether North Asia tech conviction (relevant to the owner's exposure) survives the break, the Iran escalation, or whether profit-taking resumes.
